news.story: The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. news.story: Estime's role in the offense was reduced in Week 10 against the Panthers, which marked Travis Etienne's return from a five-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Estime is a healthy scratch for Sunday's game, which means Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson will operate as the rotational options out of the backfield behind Etienne. Estime's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

news.story: White showed up on the Commanders' Week 11 injury report Friday as limited due to a heel issue and then didn't practice Saturday, leaving him questionable to play Monday. While he's confirmed to be available, he also will be welcoming back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) from IR for the first time since Week 5, which may eat into White's workload.

The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

news.story: Despite being on the field for only 25 of the Jaguars' 68 offensive snaps in Week 11, Cameron drew a career-high seven targets. He wasn't terribly efficient on those targets, but neither was Jacksonville's offense as a whole Sunday. He'll be lining up against a much softer pass defense in a Week 12 tilt versus the Titans.

The reigning NFL rushing yards leader continues to put up stellar production heading into Thursday night's home game against the Chiefs.

Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on…

news.headline: Marks (concussion) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
news.story: Marks didn't practice last week before being ruled out for this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts, but with some extra recovery time since then, the running back is trending toward a return to the lineup Sunday against the Ravens. To get there, however, he'll need to fully progress through the NFL's concussion protocol in the days leading up to the Texans' Week 12 contest.

news.headline: Marks (concussion) was on the practice field Wednesday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
news.story: Marks, who was inactive for last Thursday's game against the Colts, was, as of Monday, "trending in the right direction," according to coach DeMeco Ryans, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. The running back's presence for Wednesday's session supports that notion, with Marks' official participation level in line to provide key context ahead of this Sunday's matchup against the Ravens.

news.headline: Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Marks (concussion) is "trending in the right direction," and the Texans "are hopeful to have him" for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
news.story: After sustaining a concussion in a Nov. 15 loss to the Browns, Marks was unable to clear the five-step protocol on a short week and ended up sitting out this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts. Since then, Marks appears to have progressed on some level through the protocol, though it's not yet clear if he'll be available to practice when the Texans kick off Week 12 prep Wednesday. If Marks ends up getting the…

Warren brought in one of five targets for 22 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
news.story: The talented tight end's production continued to suffer collateral damage from Daniel Jones' poor play, but Warren did provide a useful gain on his one catch. The 2025 first-round pick now has recorded Thursday's yardage total or less in three of the last four games, but Warren's outlook may change if Jones, who James Boyd of The Athletic reports head coach Shane Steichen wouldn't rule out demoting when asked after…

news.headline: Knight carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and caught his only target for 10 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
news.story: Although he split the backfield workload nearly equally with Tyler Allgeier, Knight was the more productive RB, although he still failed to reach 50 rushing yards for a fourth straight game. The 25-year-old running back gets a more favorable matchup in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Knight and Allgeier could face additional competition for touches if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is cleared to return.

news.headline: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
news.story: Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries. The Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, however. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck…

news.headline: Franklin did not record a catch in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
news.story: The wide receiver did see two targets, but he wasn't able to haul them in. Franklin has just 17 targets across 10 games this year, recording nine catches for 100 yards and no scores.

news.headline: Dowdle rushed five times for 15 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
news.story: Dowdle finished with 34 scrimmage yards for a second consecutive game after racking up 235 scrimmage yards over his preceding four appearances. He had five more yards than Jaylen Warren on two fewer touches in Sunday's loss. Dowdle is poised to retain his spot as the 1B option alongside Warren in Friday's Week 12 home game against the Broncos.

news.headline: Felton (hip) was listed as a full participant on Thursday's injury report.
news.story: Felton was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough by a hip injury, but his ability to get back to full one day later gives him the all clear for Sunday's game versus the Falcons. Assuming Jordan Addison (thumb) misses a third consecutive contest in Week 12, Felton again will be a candidate for an expanded role, which has translated to nine catches (on 17 targets) for 75 yards the last two outings.

news.headline: Felton (hip) was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough.
news.story: Felton has had increased sway in the Vikings offense the past two games with Jordan Addison sidelined, combining for nine catches (on 17 targets) for 75 yards. Addison is trending toward another absence Sunday against the Falcons, so Felton is in line to continue his elevated role this weekend, assuming he's able to play through his hip injury.

news.headline: Felton caught six of 12 targets for 42 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
news.story: Felton was set to operate in an expanded role with Jordan Addison (thumb) on injured reserve, and he garnered a game-high 12 targets. The wide receiver finished tied for second on the team in catches with tight end T.J. Hockenson while fellow wideout Justin Jefferson (seven) led the way. Felton has caught nine of 17 targets for 75 yards over the last two weeks, and his next chance to build off of his recent…

Brissett completed 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers. He added seven rushing yards on two carries.
news.story: It was another decent showing for the veteran quarterback, and his first TD pass in two games as a Raven came on a trick that involved a direct snap to Derrick Henry, who flipped it Brissett for a 52-yard strike to Rashod Bateman. Brissett has also kept Zay Flowers relevant, feeding the wideout 18 targets for a 14-171-0 line. Baltimore's passing attack will try to keep improving in Week 12 against the Texans.

news.headline: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
news.story: Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas…

news.headline: Hutchinson caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.
news.story: Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new…

news.headline: Hutchinson is expected to continue to benefit from elevated playing time Thursday against the Colts while Marvin Harrison (hamstring) is sidelined for a second straight game, Jared Koch of SI.com reports.
news.story: Harrison hasn't exceeded a 50 percent snap share in any of his three appearances with the Texans since coming over in a trade with the Cardinals, but his absence for the Week 10 loss to the Browns still proved beneficial for Hutchinson. The fourth-year wideout out of Iowa State tied his season high with nine targets against the Browns, finishing with four catches for 58 yards and a touchdown while playing more than…

news.story: One week after taking a back seat to rookie Jordyn Tyson, Olave re-emerged as Tyler Shough's favorite downfield option, as he set a new season high in targets and topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time in 2026. news.headline: Diggs (personal) was removed from the Commanders' injury report Thursday.
news.story: Diggs had an excused absence Wednesday but avoided the injury report entirely one day later, setting him up to continue to serve as Washington's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver. Since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season due to a torn patellar tendon that he suffered in Week 6 at San Francisco, Diggs has compiled a 16-217-2 line on 27 targets over the last four games.

Diggs was absent from Wednesday's practice and was excused, Ben Standig of The Team 980 reports.
news.story: Diggs was away from the team for Wednesday's session due to a personal issue. There's no indication this will be a long-term absence, and the Commanders did excuse him for Wednesday. Still, Diggs' return to the team will be worth monitoring over the coming days in advance of Sunday's game at Arizona.

news.story: Kittle scored on both of his first-half catches, capping San Francisco's opening drive with a 17-yard touchdown before adding an eight-yard score in the first minute of the second quarter. The multi-touchdown performance was especially impressive considering the Vikings came in having allowed just one touchdown on a league-low 33 catches to tight ends. Kittle has been one of the top performers at his position as…

news.headline: Bowers (ankle) remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
news.story: The star tight end, who was inactive this past Sunday against the Broncos, has now strung together four straight limited practices, which bodes well for his chances of being back for this weekend's game against the Browns. Friday's final injury report will determine whether Bowers carries an injury designation for the contest or is fully cleared for Week 12 action.

news.headline: Bowers (ankle) was on the field for Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Bowers, who was inactive versus Denver in Week 11, logged his third straight limited practice Wednesday, which offers hope that the star TE will be available this weekend against the Browns. Per McFadden, Bowers' right ankle was heavily wrapped up Thursday, which wasn't the case the day before. The Raiders' upcoming injury report will clarify his official participation level in Wednesday' session, in any case.

news.headline: Head coach Klint Kubiak said that Bowers (ankle) remained a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but the Raiders are optimistic that the tight end will play Sunday against the Browns, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Bowers was sidelined for this past Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos, but he's now practiced in a limited fashion in each of the Raiders' last three sessions. Though the Raiders have a bye looming in Week 13 that would give Bowers more time to recover from his lower-body injuries, Kubiak indicated that the break in the schedule won't be a factor in Bowers' status for this Sunday's matchup with the Browns, per Ryan…

news.headline: Waller (knee) was listed as limited on Thursday's estimated injury report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: For s second week in a row, Waller is dealing with a knee injury, but his listing to begin this week implies he's a bit healthier after kicking off Week 11 prep with a DNP. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in full Friday and Saturday before the Panthers potentially make a call on his status for Monday's game at Tampa Bay.

news.headline: Waller caught all three of his targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
news.story: The veteran tight end was out-produced by second-year player Mitchell Evans, who posted a 5-44-1 line on five targets, but Waller made more of an impact than Tommy Tremble, who caught his only target for 18 yards. With all three members of the trio capable of making a splash in any given week, Waller will be tough to rely on heading into a Week 12 meeting with the Buccaneers.

news.headline: Waller (knee) is listed as active Sunday against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
news.story: The Panthers kicked off Week 11 prep with their top two tight ends (Waller and Tommy Tremble) not practicing due to knee injuries, after which head coach Dave Canales told Steve Reed of the Associated Press that those issues were a "concern." Both Waller and Tremble were limited Thursday and Friday and entered the weekend listed as questionable. Now that Waller is confirmed to be active -- along with Tremble -- the…

news.headline: McMillan (foot) was listed as a DNP on Thursday's practice estimate, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: After McMillan didn't participate in Wednesday's unofficial practice due to a sore foot, head coach Dave Canales told Kaye that the team is "optimistic" that the wide receiver will play Monday at Tampa Bay. McMillan will have two more chances to mix into drills this week before the Panthers potentially tag him with a designation for Week 12 action.

news.headline: Head coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that the Panthers are "optimistic" that McMillan (foot) will play Monday in Tampa Bay, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: McMillan didn't partake in Wednesday's unofficial practice, after which Canales revealed that the wide receiver dealt with soreness in his foot after Sunday's win against the Ravens in which he hauled in six of nine targets for 71 yards and one touchdown. Considering the Panthers likely are practicing Wednesday in lieu of a session on Thanksgiving, McMillan appears set to be listed as a DNP on the team's first Week…

news.headline: McMillan wasn't spotted at Wednesday's unofficial practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Because the Panthers don't play until Monday at Tampa Bay, they won't be posting an injury report until Thursday, at which point a reason for practice restrictions, if any, for McMillan will become known. According to Person, McMillan limped off the field during this past Sunday's win against the Ravens but returned to action, so he may be dealing with a health concern as Carolina begins Week 12 prep.

news.headline: Rice secured all six targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.story: Rice tied for the team lead in receptions and finished as the runner-up in targets to Travis Kelce. The veteran receiver averaged a modest 8.8 yards per catch, his third game in the last four with under 10.0 yards per reception. Rice has at least five catches in four consecutive contests heading into Thursday's Week 12 Thanksgiving showdown against the Bills in Buffalo.

news.headline: Fantasy buzz: How to navigate your roster for the Thanksgiving slate
Downs brought in four of five targets for 59 yards in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.story: Playing in his second game as a member of the Chiefs, Downs posted four receptions for the second consecutive contest and upped his receiving yardage total by six over that of his team debut. Downs' quick chemistry with Patrick Mahomes is certainly noteworthy and makes an already impressive air attack all the more effective heading into Thursday night's Thanksgiving road showdown against the Bills.

news.headline: Which of these 15 pass catchers should you trust going forward?
Coleman caught two of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 26-9 win over Miami.
news.story: Coleman finished with fewer than 20 receiving yards for the fourth straight week, and he hasn't reached the end zone since Week 6. The wide receiver has operated in a limited role on offense since DJ Moore returned to action in Week 8 following a shoulder injury, and Coleman will remain an unattractive fantasy asset ahead of the team's matchup with the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

news.headline: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
news.story: Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable…

news.headline: Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for three yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
news.story: Cook extended his touchdown streak to nine games with a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. He accounted for all but five of Buffalo's rushing attempts as Josh Allen finished without one, but Cook came up short of 100 scrimmage yards for the first time since Week 4. The reigning NFL rushing yards leader continues to put up stellar production heading into Thursday night's home game against the Chiefs.

news.headline: Bryant caught three passes for 32 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
news.story: The wideout briefly exited the game in the third quarter after he appeared to tweak his previously injured ankle, but Bryant quickly returned and was able to finish out the contest. His four targets were fourth on the team on a day Bo Nix targeted nine different players on 35 pass attempts. The Denver offense spreads the ball around to five different receivers, three tight ends and its running backs most weeks,…

news.headline: Bryant returned to Sunday's game against the Raiders after making a brief visit to the sideline tent, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
news.story: Bryant's time away from the field occurred in the middle of the third quarter. He'll look to build upon the 3-32-0 line on three targets that he accrued to that point in the contest.

news.story: Freiermuth matched his season high in catches, securing five passes in a game for the third time this year. The tight end has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards in a contest this season, and he entered Week 11 with exactly two catches in each of the team's last four games. Freiermuth has now caught 32 of 43 targets for 309 yards and five touchdowns while also adding four rushes for five yards and a score over 10…

news.headline: Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown while catching his lone target for 13 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
news.story: Jones tied the game with an 11-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, but the 49ers outscored the Vikings 21-3 in the second quarter, forcing Minnesota into a more pass-heavy approach. Jordan Mason led the team with 38 rushing yards on 11 carries. Jones and Mason should continue to split carries in Week 12 against the Falcons, with Jones offering greater upside as a pass catcher.

Ridley caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
news.story: Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

news.headline: Ridley played four offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
news.story: Even though Carnell Tate (shoulder) was sidelined for a second consecutive week, Ridley was barely involved in the Titans' offensive game plan. Ridley's four offensive snaps were by far a season low, and his role figures to shrink even more given that Tate is expected to return for Week 11 against the Cowboys on Nov. 22. Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) could be sidelined for that contest, although those offensive snaps…

news.headline: Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. He also rushed once for four yards.
news.story: Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. Smith threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Breece Hall to snap the Jets' two-game touchdown drought in the second quarter, then tacked on touchdown passes of eight and 15 yards to…

news.headline: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
news.story: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

news.headline: Smith (ankle) will practice Friday, and head coach Aaron Glenn said "things look promising for him playing Sunday," Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
news.story: While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. The Jets' final injury report will reveal whether or not Smith carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

Both Hall and Braelon Allen (17 touches for 84 yards) were heavily involved as the Jets snapped a five-game losing streak and were able to stick with the ground game. news.story: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining sidelined for Week 11, Bernard retained his every-down role on offense, playing 67 of 71 offensive snaps while leading the team in routes (52) and targets. It was a nice bounce-back game for the rookie after he was held without a catch on three targets against the Bengals in Week 10. Pittman is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, but Bernard could keep pacing…

news.headline: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
news.story: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

news.headline: Restrepo was signed to the Titans' active roster Tuesday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official website reports.
news.story: Restrepo was elevated to the active roster in Week 10 against the Jaguars, and he reeled in all three of his targets for 31 yards over 19 offensive snaps. After fellow wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Restrepo will replace him on the active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cowboys.

news.story: Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. news.headline: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
news.story: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

news.headline: Smith (ankle) will practice Friday, and head coach Aaron Glenn said "things look promising for him playing Sunday," Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
news.story: While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. The Jets' final injury report will reveal whether or not Smith carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

news.headline: Taylor caught two passes for 25 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
news.story: The Jets controlled this game from start to finish and never trailed, so Geno Smith attempted just 21 passes to 37 run plays for New York. Taylor's 25 yards were his most in a game since Week 7, and he's totaled just 10 catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns over his last four contests. He's a very risky play as a fantasy tight end.

news.headline: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Taylor could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers.
news.story: Isaiah Williams (ribs) also has been ruled out for the Jets, so they'll be down their Nos. 3 and 4 receivers, which could lead to more multiple-tight end sets for New York. Taylor is averaging 2.8 catches for 20.9 yards per game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

news.headline: Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
news.story: Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games…

news.story: Coker sustained the injury on a six-yard catch with 1:58 remaining in the fourth quarter, when he appeared to bear the brunt of a helmet-to-helmet hit. Prior to his departure, Coker recorded four receptions for 47 yards on seven targets. His status will be worth monitoring heading into the Panthers' Nov. 30 matchup with the Buccaneers in Week 12.

news.headline: Nailor caught one of five targets for 16 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.
news.story: Nailor caught one pass for the second straight week, and he has exceeded 20 receiving yards only one time since Week 1. Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-33 win over Baltimore.
news.story: The fourth-year QB posted his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3 percent) while tossing multiple TDs for the third time in the last six contests, a stretch in which he's compiled a 9:5 TD:INT. Both of Young's scores came in the first half, as he connected with Mitchell Evans on a 23-yard TD and Tetairoa McMillan on a seven-yard strike. Young will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against Tampa Bay.

news.headline: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice.
news.story: Per Steve Reed of the Associated Press, head coach Dave Canales said that Young experienced some soreness in his foot coming out of Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. However, after receiving treatment over the last couple of days, Young responded well enough to take every rep in practice to kick off Week 11 prep. The signal-caller isn't expected to face any limitations during this Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

news.story: This past Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston indicated that the hip injury Boutte suffered in last Thursday's win over the Colts didn't appear to be serious. However, with a DNP to start the practice week, the wideout's status will need to be monitored as Sunday's game against the Ravens approaches. Apart from a 4-125-2 receiving line in a 44-22 win over the Chargers in Week 9, Boutte has produced modest…

news.headline: Boutte's hip injury he suffered in Thursday night's win over the Colts doesn't appear to be serious, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
news.story: The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

news.headline: Virgil wasn't targeted in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
news.story: The 22-year-old wide receiver played just two offensive snaps, the same amount as Devin Duvernay, as the duo played behind all three of Simi Fehoko (52 snaps), Harrison Wallace (36) and Zay Jones (32) in the Cardinals' injury-ravaged wideout depth chart. Virgil has three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets across seven games this season and therefore doesn't possess any fantasy relevance at the moment.

news.headline: Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't get a target during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
news.story: The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, finishing with just 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers,…

news.headline: Fehoko caught one of five targets for a two-yard touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
news.story: The wideout led his position group by playing 52 of 56 offensive snaps, and he ran a team-high 34 routes on Josh Johnson's 37 dropbacks. It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows…

news.headline: Fehoko finished Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams with one catch on two targets for 21 yards. He also recorded a tackle.
news.story: Week 10 was the Cardinals' first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck as the starting quarterback. The offense struggled to move the ball and logged only 35 snaps as a whole while finishing with 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Fehoko and the rest of the Cardinals' skill-position players, although the sixth-year pro did connect with Beck on a 21-yard pass early in the first…

news.headline: Juszczyk caught both of his targets for 13 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
news.story: Juszczyk was able to reel in his first two passes since Week 7, notching his fourth multi-catch performance of the year. The fullback has now caught 10 of 13 targets for 89 yards and two touchdowns while also adding a four-yard rush over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

news.headline: Sarratt (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina.
news.story: Sarratt has been active for two games this season, most recently appearing in Week 4 versus the Titans. Since then, he's been held out. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 versus the Texans.

news.headline: Quitoriano played all 13 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
news.story: Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense…

news.headline: Watkins caught one of his three targets for 26 yards during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
news.story: Watkins played just five offensive snaps for the Colts in Thursday night's game. Despite playing only 10 percent of the offensive snaps, Watkins totaled the third-highest yardage by Colts pass catchers on the night with his 26-yard grab. The reserve wide receiver could see an expanded role down the stretch as the Colts experiment with starting quarterback Anthony Richardson in what is all but a lost season.

news.headline: The Colts signed Watkins from their practice squad to their 53-man roster Tuesday.
news.story: A spot on the 53-man roster opened up when Indianapolis placed linebacker Jaylon Carlies (neck) on IR, and the team elected to give Watkins the opening. The veteran wideout was elevated for Sunday's Week 10 win over Miami, but he didn't end up playing. With that said, there could be an opportunity for Watkins to garner some work in the passing game after Indianapolis traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs and Keenan Allen…

news.headline: Watkins reverted to the Colts' practice squad Monday.
news.story: Watkins was active for Sunday's win over the Dolphins but didn't play any snaps. The wide receiver has two more practice-squad elevations remaining this season before he would need to be signed to the Colts' 53-man roster in order to suit up on game days.

news.headline: Coleman failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
news.story: With Chris Bell (knee) back from his absence, Coleman reverted to WR4 duties for Miami, playing just 12 of 57 offensive snaps. He has no fantasy appeal while Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington and Bell are healthy. Coleman has been extremely inefficient through 10 games this season, catching just nine of 28 targets for 88 yards and two touchdowns.

news.headline: Coleman logged one catch for six yards on six targets in Sunday's Week 10 loss to Indianapolis.
news.story: Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.

news.headline: Tolbert caught his only target for 17 yards during Sunday's 26-9 loss at Buffalo.
news.story: Tolbert played just eight of the Dolphins' 55 offensive snaps in Week 11, and he drew just one target for the third time in his last five games. Miami will probably continue to lean primarily on Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell at wide receiver in a Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.

news.headline: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
news.story: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle…

news.headline: Thompson (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
news.story: Thompson has not played since the Chargers' Week 2 game with the Raiders. The wide receiver initially dealt with a quadriceps injury before sustaining a hamstring injury while still recovering. Thompson's long string of DNPs continues into Week 12 prep, and it appears there may be no end in sight.

news.headline: Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
news.story: Thompson's inactive status doesn't come as much of a surprise, given that he entered the weekend as doubtful due to a hamstring injury. He hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders, and his next chance to see the field is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

news.headline: Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Jets.
news.story: Thompson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury and has not seen regular-season action since Week 2 against the Raiders. If he's ruled out for Sunday's game, then the rookie fourth-rounder's next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

news.headline: The Steelers placed Skowronek (calf) on injured reserve Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
news.story: Skowronek has been working through a calf issue since mid-October, and he appeared to aggravate the injury during the Steelers' Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Now that he's on injured reserve, Skowronek will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 27. Max Hurleman was signed off the practice squad to the 53-man roster in a…

news.headline: Skowronek (calf) did not practice Tuesday.
news.story: The 29-year-old appears to have suffered a setback with his calf injury, as he opened Week 12 as a non-participant in practice Tuesday. Skowronek missed the Steelers' last three games due to the same injury. He will likely need to upgrade his practice status for a chance to play Friday against the Broncos.

news.headline: Jefferson failed to haul in his lone target during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.
news.story: Jefferson could not hold onto a deep pass from Jayden Daniels early in the fourth quarter, and that catch would have set up the Commanders in the red zone. Jefferson has seen only one pass across his two outings since putting together a 5-58-1 receiving line on seven targets against the Rams in Week 9. Jefferson is firmly entrenched as the Commanders' WR4 behind Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks…

news.headline: Walker recorded 211 kickoff-return yards, including an 86-yard touchdown, and one catch for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
news.story: The wide receiver filled a returner role for the first time this season and did well. Walker has seen just 10 targets on offense in 2026, so he's not much of a factor in fantasy leagues at the moment, but he could garner more opportunities on special teams following Sunday's success.

news.headline: Legette did not play an offensive snap in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
news.story: The wide receiver did play nine snaps on special teams. Legette missed six games with a knee injury before returning for Carolina's win over the Saints in Week 10, though he only saw action on two offensive snaps in that contest. Legette has two catches for 64 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season.

news.headline: Legette didn't produce any output in the boxscore during Carolina's win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.story: Legette made his return to the lineup after having been sidelined since Week 2 due to a knee injury, but he ended up playing just two snaps on offense. He will look to be more involved during next week's matchup versus the Ravens.

news.headline: Lambert-Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
news.story: With Ladd McConkey (back) active, Lambert-Smith will be a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest. Lambert-Smith's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29, although his path to playing time is limited unless there is an injury in front of him on the Chargers' wide receiver depth chart.

news.headline: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.
news.story: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown…

news.headline: Singletary finished with one carry for five yards and one catch for five yards in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.
news.story: The running back played just 10 offensive snaps behind starter Cam Skattebo. Singletary has averaged just 2.9 yards per carry this year on 41 attempts.

news.headline: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday.
news.story: Shepard was elevated for Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers due to the absences of fellow wideouts Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs). The veteran receiver answered the call by hauling in both of his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Since Shepard has now been elevated the maximum three times, he'll need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up again for the Jets this…

news.headline: Shepard caught two passes for 24 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
news.story: With Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) inactive, Shepard was elevated from the practice squad and logged 22 of 60 offensive snaps. He ran 13 routes on Geno Smith's 23 dropbacks and obviously made the most of his two targets. In his 120th career regular-season game, it was Shepard's first career two-touchdown performance. It's unlikely to be indicative of future performance.

news.headline: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
news.story: The move gives the Jets much-needed depth at wide receiver given the absences of both Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Sunday's game against the Chargers. It will be the third elevation of the season for Shepard and first since Week 4 against the Bears, so he would need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up for the Jets beyond Week 11.

news.headline: Cooper (ankle/groin) was listed as a non-participant in practice Thursday.
news.story: Cooper also logged a 'DNP' on Wednesday's practice estimate, so what -- if anything -- he's able to do Friday will be pivotal with regard to his status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If Cooper is sidelined for a second straight time this weekend, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams, in that order, would be next up for added opportunities at WR for the Jets versus Miami.

news.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Cooper (ankle/hip) won't practice Wednesday and is considered day-to-day.
news.story: The rookie wide receiver will be sidelined for a fourth consecutive practice while he continues to manage a pair of injuries, but the Jets aren't closing the door on Cooper putting an end to a one-game absence and playing this Sunday in Miami. In order to put himself in a position to suit up this weekend, however, Cooper will likely need to put in a full practice either Thursday or Friday. If Cooper ends up missing…

news.headline: Coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Cooper (ankle/hip) will be out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
news.story: Cooper didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a pair of injuries, and he'll wind up sitting out Week 11. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will be the primary wideouts for the Jets, and with Isaiah Williams (ribs) joining Cooper on the sidelines, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick will be options when the team wants to get more receivers on the field, and per head coach Aaron Glenn -- via Rich Cimini of ESPN.com…

news.headline: Winston carried twice for one yard in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
news.story: J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. He extended a second-quarter drive that culminated in a Cam Skattebo touchdown by gaining a yard on a fourth-and-one play, but Winston was dropped for no gain on a third-and-one run in the fourth quarter that resulted in a Giants punt. The Giants may continue to…

news.headline: Wayne (quadriceps) didn't practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
news.story: Wayne has missed the Dolphins' last two games due to a quadriceps injury. He would need to practice in at least a limited capacity over the next two days to have a realistic chance of being available for Sunday's game against the Jets.

news.headline: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
news.story: Wayne will miss a second straight game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29. In his absence, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will serve as the Dolphins' rotational wide receivers behind Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell.

news.headline: Wayne (quadriceps) did not participate at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
news.story: Wayne sat out Sunday's game at Indianapolis with a quad injury, and his availability for Week 11 is now in question. If he's not able to get back onto the practice field Thursday or Friday, he'll be trending toward missing Sunday's game at Buffalo.

news.headline: Watkins (groin) was estimated as a 'DNP' on Thursday's injury report, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
news.story: The 49ers didn't hold a practice for Thanksgiving Day, but Watkins has been listed as a non-participant for the first two sessions of Week 12 prep due to a groin injury. He has one more opportunity to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks. In the event that Watkins is not cleared to play against Seattle, more offensive snaps would be available for the likes of Jacob…

news.headline: Watkins (groin) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
news.story: Watkins may have injured his groin during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings in Week 11, when he hauled in his lone target for 19 yards while playing 28 snaps on offense. His practice participation over the next two days will shed light on his status heading into Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Seahawks. If Watkins cannot play in Week 12, then Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson would all be in…

news.headline: Watkins brought in his lone target for 19 yards during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday.
news.story: Watkins' 28 offensive snaps were tied with Deebo Samuel for second most among 49ers wide receivers behind Keenan Allen (31) and ahead of Mike Evans (23). Watkins has played at least 50 percent of San Francisco's offensive snaps in each of the team's last five games, but the second-year pro is stuck in a complementary role on offense behind Evans, Allen, Samuel, tight end George Kittle and running back Christian…

news.headline: Shavers failed to bring in either of his two targets and logged one tackle on kick coverage in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
news.story: Shavers played 27 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams in his return to the field Sunday. The wide receiver has finally started to mix into the offense after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in the Bills' 27-24 wild-card win over the Jaguars last January.

news.headline: Shavers (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
news.story: Shavers was activated from the reserve/PUP list Saturday, and the San Diego State product has been officially cleared to play Sunday in what will be his first game since the Bills AFC wild-card round win over the Jaguars in January, when he tore his ACL. Shavers will likely operate in a rotational role on offense behind DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman.

news.headline: Bills head coach Joe Brady said Wednesday that Shavers (knee) has been reinstated from the PUP list, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
news.story: Shavers' 21-day evaluation window was set to close this week, so the Bills elected to add him back to the 53-man roster to ensure that he would be available to play this season. The wideout has been a full practice participant for the past two weeks, so he appears to be fully recovered from the torn ACL he sustained in January and should be available for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If active for the Week 11…

news.headline: Jennings caught three of six targets for 20 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
news.story: Jennings made his return to action after missing two games with a calf injury. The 29-year-old reeled in a season-high three passes, while his six targets were also the most he's had in a game this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 40 receiving yards in contest, and Jennings hasn't scored a touchdown this season. His next chance to accomplish both feats will come in Week 12 versus the Falcons.

news.headline: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.
news.story: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this…

news.headline: Moreau brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
news.story: Moreau's 30 offensive snaps were second among Texans tight ends behind Dalton Schultz's 34, yet it was Marlin Klein who led the position group with four catches (on as many targets) for 24 yards, including a 13-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud late in the third quarter. Moreau is up to a 12-80-3 receiving line on 15 targets through 10 regular-season games and has caught one pass or zero in five of those…

news.headline: McCord completed 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills. He also rushed twice for nine yards.
news.story: McCord has thrown for just 311 yards without a touchdown pass in his first two NFL starts. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles is poised to make at least two more starts while Malik Willis (abdomen) is on IR. Miami's lone win of the season came against the Jets, whom the Dolphins will host in Week 12.

news.headline: The Seahawks placed Holani (knee) on injured reserve Monday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
news.story: Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back…

news.headline: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Bills, Johnson is once again set to lead the Chiefs' backfield.
news.story: The Chiefs are on a short week, so the team elected to err on the side of caution with Walker, setting the stage for Johnson to log his third straight start at RB for the team. The 2026 fifth-rounder thus remains an extremely viable Week 12 fantasy lineup option. In both of his previous turns in a starting capacity, Johnson has exceeded 100 rushing yards while adding 10 catches and three total TDs in that span.

Emmett Johnson could be a flex option even when Kenneth Walker III returns
Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.
news.story: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

news.headline: Young caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Monday night's 22-20 loss to the Commanders.
news.story: Young reeled in his first pass since Week 3, and he notched his first career touchdown in the process. The wide receiver connected with quarterback Joe Burrow for a four-yard score in the third quarter, momentarily providing Cincinnati with a 17-10 lead. Young's 22 offensive snaps ranked third at his position behind Ja'Marr Chase (56) and Tee Higgins (56) while ahead of Dohnte Meyers (21), but Young may revert to a…

news.headline: Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
news.story: Week 11 marks the fifth time in six games that Singleton will be a healthy scratch, despite the fact that Tyjae Spears (knee) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. As such, Michael Carter and Julius Chestnut will operate as the Titans' rotational options in the backfield behind workhorse running back Tony Pollard on Sunday. Singleton's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Nov. 29.

news.headline: The Chargers signed Wease to their practice squad Thursday.
news.story: Wease was waived Tuesday, but he went unclaimed and will remain with Los Angeles as part of the practice squad. The 25-year-old has played in four games this season, tallying three catches for 37 yards on five targets.

news.headline: Wease was waived by the Chargers on Tuesday.
news.story: Wease was signed to the active roster with Los Angeles on Oct. 10, and he caught three of five targets for 37 yards while appearing in four contests with the team before being let go Tuesday. The wide receiver will likely land on the Chargers' practice squad.

news.headline: Lance failed to catch his only target and added 47 yards on kickoff returns during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
news.story: Lance was unable to reel in a deep pass from quarterback Tyler Shough in the first quarter, and he didn't get another look the rest of the game. The wide receiver was on the field for 21 offensive snaps, ranking fourth at his position behind Devaughn Vele (64), Chris Olave (62) and Jordyn Tyson (36) in the contest. Lance will continue to primarily serve as a special-teams asset for New Orleans moving forward,…

news.headline: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.story: The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears…

news.headline: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Bills, Johnson is once again set to lead the Chiefs' backfield.
news.story: The Chiefs are on a short week, so the team elected to err on the side of caution with Walker, setting the stage for Johnson to log his third straight start at RB for the team. The 2026 fifth-rounder thus remains an extremely viable Week 12 fantasy lineup option. In both of his previous turns in a starting capacity, Johnson has exceeded 100 rushing yards while adding 10 catches and three total TDs in that span.

Emmett Johnson could be a flex option even when Kenneth Walker III returns
Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
news.story: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

news.headline: Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
news.story: Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any…

Allen caught two of four targets for 41 yards during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals.
news.story: Allen was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after having done so only twice in the team's first eight games of the year. The wide receiver played 16 offensive snaps which ranked sixth at his position behind Xavier Worthy (47), Rashee Rice (32), Jalen Royals (24), Andrew Armstrong (20) and Josh Downs (17). As a result of the depth of the WR room in Kansas City, Allen will remain a hard…

news.headline: Humphrey (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.
news.story: Humphrey will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Steelers on Black Friday, although Humphrey is unlikely to see the field unless a wide receiver ahead of him on the depth chart is not available.

news.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Grab your Rams and Packers quickly
Mendoza was 18-for-37 passing for 267 yards, three touchdowns and one interception and had four carries for 22 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss in Denver.
news.story: After throwing for no touchdowns or interceptions in his first NFL start last Sunday against the Seahawks, Mendoza recorded the first scoring strike of his career on a 68-yard catch and run via RB Ashton Jeanty in Week 11. Mendoza also hooked up with Ian Thomas (19 yards) and Jack Bech (seven yards) for his other two TDs, but he followed up a 58.6 completion percentage in Week 10 with more misfires (19) than…

news.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Replacing Drake Maye? Trust in Tyson?
Allen logged 80 kickoff-return yards in the Dolphins' 26-9 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
news.story: Allen played 16 special-teams snaps in the contest. The running back did not log an offensive snap, leaving all the rushing work to Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright.

news.headline: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
news.story: Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

news.headline: Bell (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
news.story: Bell made his third appearance of the 2026 campaign in Week 10, though he went without a catch. With Tyrell Shavers (knee) cleared to play for Sunday's divisional clash with Miami after spending time on injured reserve, Bell's services won't be needed. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 against the Chiefs.

news.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Grab your Rams and Packers quickly
Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
news.story: Freiermuth matched his season high in catches, securing five passes in a game for the third time this year. The tight end has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards in a contest this season, and he entered Week 11 with exactly two catches in each of the team's last four games. Freiermuth has now caught 32 of 43 targets for 309 yards and five touchdowns while also adding four rushes for five yards and a score over 10…

news.story: Iosivas will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week, after the Bengals had listed him as doubtful heading into Monday's contest following a trio of full practices from Thursday through Saturday. If the fourth-year wideout can turn in another full slate of practices in Week 12, he should have a better chance of being restored to the 53-man roster ahead of the Bengals' Nov. 29 matchup with the Saints.

news.headline: Iosivas (thumb) is listed as doubtful for Monday's game against the Commanders.
news.story: Iosivas was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but it looks like the fourth-year wide receiver will stay on injured reserve for at least one more week while recovering from a thumb injury. If he's inactive for Monday's game, then his next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday, Nov. 29.

news.headline: Iosivas (thumb) practiced fully Thursday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Iosivas had his 21-day practice window opened last week but remains on injured reserve. With Dohnte Meyers playing well as the Bengals' WR3, there's likely no rush to activate Iosivas, who has just 87 career regular-season catches across 52 appearances. He's averaged 20.2 receiving yards per game in his career.

In place of Beck, Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and one touchdown while also taking two carries for five yards. Friday's injury report will reveal if Beck has a chance to play in Week 12, and by proxy if Johnson will get another spot start.

news.headline: Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. he added five yards on two carries.

For however long McGowan is sidelined, Giddens figures to serve as Jonathan Taylor's backup at running back. Giddens has shown some flashes this season in limited playing time, amassing 48 yards on seven carries (6.9 YPC) and catching his only target for 11 yards over three games.

If McGowan's injury costs him time, Giddens figures to handle RB2 duties in his absence.

news.story: Giddens barely saw the field during Sunday's win, and his two offensive snaps were well behind fellow running backs Jonathan Taylor (40) and Seth McGowan (17). Giddens -- a fifth-round pick of the Colts in the 2025 NFL Draft -- has seen little playing time since making his 2026 regular-season debut in Week 8 against the Jaguars. His role will likely stay minimal for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

news.story: Isaiah Williams (ribs) also has been ruled out for the Jets, so they'll be down their Nos. 3 and 4 receivers, which could lead to more multiple-tight end sets for New York. Taylor is averaging 2.8 catches for 20.9 yards per game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

news.headline: Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
news.story: Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games…

Stroud completed 21 of 26 passes for 194 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed six times for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
news.story: Stroud's night got off to a rocky start when a deflected pass resulted in an interception on the Texans' opening drive, but the red-hot signal-caller was near perfect from that point forward. The 2023 first-round pick went on to toss three touchdown passes for the second straight game and multiple scores for the fifth consecutive contest overall. Stroud connected with Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayshon Boutte (24…

news.headline: Hibner recorded two catches for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
news.story: Hibner logged 35 of 65 snaps on offense, with his 54 percent share ranking second to only Mark Andrews (62 percent) among Ravens tight ends. The rookie fourth-round pick out of SMU's playing time has held steady between 30 and 60 percent of snaps over his 10 appearances, with Hibner drawing no more than two targets in any of those contests.

news.headline: Gray (ribs) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bills.
news.story: Though Gray was listed as a full participant on the Chiefs' injury reports both Tuesday and Wednesday, the team's TE2 will nonetheless carry a 'questionable" designation ahead of Week 12 action. With a 10-211-1 receiving line through 10 contests thus far, Gray is only an option in the deepest of fantasy formats, at least as long as Travis Kelce is available.

news.headline: Gray (ribs) was a full participant at the Chiefs' practice Tuesday.
news.story: Gray was considered to be a nonparticipant at the team's walkthrough practice Monday due to an injury to his ribs, but he now appears to be good to go for Week 12. The 27-year-old will operate in his primary reserve role behind Travis Kelce at tight end Thursday versus the Bills.

news.headline: Gray (ribs) was deemed a non-participant in Monday's walkthrough.
news.story: Kansas City didn't actually practice Monday, but Gray's DNP tag is nonetheless concerning with the club set to take the field Thursday versus Buffalo. Gray was injured late in Sunday's win over Arizona and didn't re-enter the contest. If the veteran tight end isn't able to suit up against the Bills, Jake Briningstool could see more work on offense as Travis Kelce's backup.

news.headline: McCord completed 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills. He also rushed twice for nine yards.
news.story: McCord has thrown for just 311 yards without a touchdown pass in his first two NFL starts. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles is poised to make at least two more starts while Malik Willis (abdomen) is on IR. Miami's lone win of the season came against the Jets, whom the Dolphins will host in Week 12.

news.headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Johnson is preparing to start Sunday's game versus the Commanders due to Carson Beck's back injury, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
news.story: Beck won't practice Wednesday due to continued issues with back spasms, which held him out of this past Sunday's loss in Kansas City. In place of Beck, Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and one touchdown while also taking two carries for five yards. Friday's injury report will reveal if Beck has a chance to play in Week 12, and by proxy if Johnson will get another spot start.

news.headline: Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. he added five yards on two carries.
news.story: The 40-year-old QB was pressed into duty with rookie Carson Beck (back) on the shelf, and Johnson unsurprisingly wasn't really up to the task after the Cardinals fell into a 14-0 hole before the first quarter was over. Johnson spent most of his afternoon finding Trey McBride for short gains, and he did hit Simi Fehoko for a two-yard score in the second quarter. Beck doesn't figure to miss much time, but if Johnson…

news.story: Coming out of his first NFL start in a Week 10 loss to the Rams, Beck was added to the injury report Thursday due to back spasms. He was listed questionable after failing to practice Friday before the Cardinals offically ruled him out for Week 11 a day later. news.story: Mahomes was clicking early against the Cardinals' defense, capping off the opening possession of the game with an eight-yard touchdown toss to Travis Kelce. The prolific signal-caller went on to add a 22-yard scoring pass to Kelce shortly before the end of the first half, and he capped off his day with an 18-yarder to Xavier Worthy on which the speedy receiver raced up the right sideline and into the end zone.…

news.headline: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich.
news.story: The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. news.story: Head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Darnold will start Sunday at San Francisco if he fares well in practice this week, and a full practice is a good place for the quarterback to kick things off. Darnold has missed the last two contests due to a quad injury and cracked ribs, but only the first concern was mentioned on Wednesday's practice report, indicating his improved level…

news.headline: Head coach Mike Macdonald reiterated that Darnold (quadriceps/rib) will start Sunday against the 49ers if the quarterback fares well during Wednesday's practice, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Darnold missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to a pair of injuries, but he appears to be feeling healthier coming out of a Week 11 bye. While Macdonald stopped just short of confirming him the team's Week 12 starter, Darnold should get the nod if he's able to practice without restrictions Wednesday and occurs no setbacks along the way.

news.headline: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Darnold (quadriceps/rib) made a "good bit of progress" over the Seahawks' Week 11 bye and will start Sunday at San Francisco if he fares well during Wednesday's practice, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Darnold has been sidelined for the Seahawks' last two games due to a quad issue and a cracked rib, but he was back on the field Monday for a bonus practice coming out of the bye week. While Macdonald relayed that Darnold "looked great" and took "a ton of reps" during what the coach referred to as more of a walk-through session, the Seahawks want to see how the veteran quarterback responds to a full-speed practice…

news.headline: Harrison (hamstring) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
news.story: Harrison has missed the Texans' last two contests, but after a limited practice Wednesday, the wideout's full participation Thursday sets the stage for him to return to action Sunday against the Ravens. news.story: Harrison has been sidelined for the Texans' last two contests, but the WR's ability to practice Wednesday, albeit in a limited fashion, bodes well for his chances of being available for Sunday's game against the Ravens. news.headline: Harrison (hamstring) was at practice Wednesday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
news.story: Harrison has missed two straight games, but his looming practice participation, in any capacity, is a good sign regarding his availability as Sunday's game against the Ravens approaches. The Texans' upcoming injury report will reveal the wideout's official participation level in Wednesday's session.
